page.title: OpenAI’s mathematics release, read and checked
page.description: Every family of OpenAI’s mathematics release drawn as one map: open a family to read what its papers claim, the Lean that states it, and who has checked what.
page.lede: An independent atlas: every family in the release is drawn here as a small map of its papers, theorems and Lean statements, and opens to show what it claims and who has checked it.
page.noscript: The map needs JavaScript. The list of every family, paper, theorem and Lean statement is below the map, with links.
page.redirect_text: The map of the release is now the front page.

legend.heading: How to read the map
legend.colour_note: Colour marks evidence, and each colour comes with a shape. Structure stays grey.
legend.lean_3: Three outside groups report accepting its re-run
legend.lean_0: No group reports accepting it yet
legend.lean_holes: Some of its definitions are checked by name and type only (the hole)
legend.lean_groups: The groups are {groups}. The atlas did not re-run these files itself.
legend.result_paired: Has a candidate Lean statement, joined by a dashed thread
legend.pair_note: Candidates are found automatically by word overlap, and nobody has reviewed them yet.
legend.family_hol: A HOL Light check of some of its steps
legend.family_finite: An exact computation of a finite part
legend.fibre_note: A fibre joins two families when a manuscript of one cites a manuscript of the other. Its width grows with the number of citing links.
legend.tiles: Every family as a tile, coloured by the evidence you choose

ways.heading: Where to start

items.why: Erdős conjectured that a set of positive integers whose reciprocals add up to infinity contains arithmetic progressions of every length. These papers claim a proof.
items.name: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture

items.why: The papers claim that no Dirichlet L-function, the Riemann zeta function included, has a zero whose real part exceeds 7/8.
items.name: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis

items.why: Penrose’s inequality bounds the mass of a spacetime below by the minimum area enclosing its black holes. These papers claim it in every dimension from three up.
items.name: The spacetime Penrose inequality

items.why: Borsuk asked whether every bounded set in n dimensions splits into n + 1 pieces of smaller diameter. The paper claims a set in dimension nine that does not.
items.name: Borsuk’s conjecture in dimension nine

ways.key_lean: A Lean statement, darker the more outside groups report accepting its re-run
ways.key_result: A headline theorem, filled when a candidate Lean statement is paired with it
ways.key_ring: A brick ring: an outside check of the family by another method

bands.example_intro: Every family page answers the same questions in the same order: what is claimed, what the Lean states, who has checked it, and where to read it. Here is one.
bands.release_s1: OpenAI published {papers} current papers, grouped into {families} families of related results in {disciplines} disciplines.
bands.release_s2: {lean} Lean statement files come with the release, in {families_with_lean} of those families, and OpenAI lists {main} of them as main results.
bands.release_s3: Outside groups report re-running those files: of the {lean} files, all three groups report accepting {acc3}, and {acc0} have no accepted re-run yet.
bands.release_s4: The atlas pairs {pairs} of the Lean files with a theorem in their papers. Each pairing is a candidate found by word overlap, and nobody has reviewed it yet.
bands.release_s5: Inside the release the papers cite one another {edges} times, and outside it they cite {works} other works.
bands.release_s6: OpenAI has withdrawn {withdrawn} papers and replaced {previous} with later editions.
bands.release_numbers: Every number, with how it was counted
bands.release_tiles: Every family as a tile, coloured by the evidence you choose
bands.checked_intro: Each check below is reported by the person or group named. The atlas shows their records beside the results they reach and did not repeat them.
bands.checked_cert: re-ran {runs} Lean files through Comparator with a second kernel and reports {accepted} accepted. They also checked finite parts of {finite} families by exact computation, and read the Lean of {scope} families against their headlines.
bands.checked_mathvet: re-ran {runs} Lean files in a sandbox and reports {accepted} accepted. They also read the Lean of {scope} families against their headlines.
bands.checked_neal: re-ran {runs} Lean files with Lean’s kernel and reports {accepted} accepted, with the time and memory each took.
bands.checked_hol: proved steps of {families} families again in HOL Light, with negative controls that must fail.
bands.checked_erdos: links {families} families to the Erdős problems they address.
bands.checked_more: Work by {efforts} other public efforts, from comments and analyses to independent checks, is credited where it is used.
bands.help_intro: Each contribution is one precise thing, credited by name on the pages it changes.
bands.help_without: Open a short form on GitHub to explain a result, check a Lean statement against its paper, or report a problem with one page.
bands.help_with: Give your assistant the start-here guide from the repository. It helps you choose one useful note, drafts it privately and leaves the signing to you.
bands.help_queue: Some Lean files have a specific reason to be read first.
